workload: 5000 independent two-sample t-tests, each over 64 observations per group, the realistic feature/hypothesis-screening usage pattern. Baseline is scipy.stats.ttest_ind called once per pair (the idiomatic way to run many independent tests). Throughput is tests/sec.

methodology.aggregation: median of repeated timed runs, warm-up excluded

gate.note: Many independent tests is the realistic batch pattern; scipy pays large per-call dispatch and result-object construction overhead that numpy cannot fuse across independent tests, while the Rust loop runs natively. A single vectorized scipy call cannot express independent unequal-membership tests, so the per-call loop is the honest comparison.

latency.note: Single-test latency ~1.05 us derived from the 949k tests/sec rate, warm-up excluded; one t-test is far under the sub-millisecond budget.

out_of_scope.stat_tests: batch-only hypothesis tests, not streaming estimators (no online formulation)

known_debt: Only the two-sample t-test is benched as the family's gated hot path; the other tests (Mann-Whitney, KS, ANOVA, chi-square, correlations, ...) share the same per-call-overhead advantage over scipy but are not separately gated.
